responsibility: This module is the GCC target backend for the FT32 architecture, responsible for turning GCC’s generic RTL and target hooks into FT32-specific code generation, ABI behavior, and assembly output. Its core files divide the work between a static target description in ft32.h, executable hook and helper logic in ft32.c/ft32.cc for calling conventions, argument and return handling, frame and prologue/epilogue generation, address legitimacy, address-space and section selection, and operand/address printing, and a declarative machine description in ft32.md that defines instruction selection, expanders, branches, moves, arithmetic, memory operations, and other RTL patterns for FT32 instructions. Supporting constraint and predicate files define the immediate classes, memory forms, and operand recognizers needed for reload, matching, and inline asm, while ft32.opt records FT32-specific command-line switches controlling features such as LRA, compressed code, program-memory placement, and instruction availability. Overall, this module encapsulates the FT32 port’s machine model, instruction set mapping, ABI rules, address-space behavior including program-memory handling, and target-specific emission policy, distinguishing it from generic middle-end code and from other architecture backends.
